corn_glutinous: Aim the spray at the lower sheaths, where the disease starts. Do not use group 11 twice in a row.
A strobilurin used alone: rotate it with a triazole so the fungus does not learn to survive it.
A strobilurin used alone: rotate it with a triazole so the fungus does not learn to survive it.

avoid: Copper hydroxide
Copper does not control the sheath blight fungus.
Mancozeb
A contact protectant that does not stop the sheath blight fungus spreading inside the canopy. Money wasted here.
Thiram
A seed treatment. It does not stop sheath blight in the standing crop.
Chlorothalonil
A contact protectant that does not control sheath blight. Money wasted here.
Bordeaux mixture
Copper does not control the sheath blight fungus.
Copper oxychloride plus copper hydroxide
Copper does not control the sheath blight fungus.
prevent: Use the right seeding rate and avoid close spacing, so air and light reach the base of the hills.
Use a moderate nitrogen rate for the season and split it. Too much nitrogen feeds the disease.
Keep weeds down in the paddy and on the bunds, since many grasses carry the fungus.
Drain the field for a few days at maximum tillering to dry the base of the hills.
After harvest, plow deep so sick stubble goes under, and skim floating trash from the water at land preparation.
In corn, strip the lowest leaves and sheaths that touch the soil, and do not plant too dense.
bio: Trichoderma harzianum attacks the fungus. Where a Trichoderma product is sold, use it early, as field results are mixed.
Bacillus products give partial control when started at maximum tillering.
diseases.threshold: From maximum tillering, part 20 hills a week and look at the sheaths near the water. Spray only when lesions keep climbing the plant and spread from hill to hill in hot, humid weather, mostly from panicle initiation to booting, and aim at the lower sheaths.
diseases.rotate: The sheath blight fungus has learned to survive strobilurins (group 11) where they were sprayed alone, so far outside Asia. Use group 11 only in a mix, never twice in a row, and rotate with triazoles (3) or SDHIs (7).

diseases.name: Rice blast
diseases.local: Mata mata (Tagalog and Bisaya), agupaw (Waray), taya taya (Cebuano in Mindanao)
diseases.hint: Spindle or diamond shaped leaf spots with gray centers and reddish brown borders.

rice: Systemic and made for blast. It protects the neck when sprayed at early heading.
Tricyclazole works before infection: spray as panicles start to emerge, and again at half heading.
Blast in Japan and Vietnam already resists strobilurins. Use it at most once a crop, then rotate.
Fungi learn to survive this group quickly. Rotate it with tricyclazole or isoprothiolane.
Fungi learn to survive this group quickly. Rotate it with tricyclazole or isoprothiolane.
Blast in Japan and Vietnam already resists strobilurins. Use it at most once a crop, then rotate.
Blast in Japan and Vietnam already resists strobilurins. Use it at most once a crop, then rotate.
Isotianil wakes the plant's own defenses. Spray before the disease shows. Do not repeat group 11.
Contact only: it guards the leaf surface for a few days and does little against neck blast.
Contact only, and some blast in Vietnam has grown less sensitive to it. Weak on neck blast.
Weak on blast, and copper can scorch rice at heading. Keep it for bacterial problems.
A friendly bacterium with only mild effect on blast. It will not hold neck blast in wet weather.
Weak on blast, and copper can scorch rice at heading. Keep it for bacterial problems.
Weak on blast, and copper can scorch rice at heading. Keep it for bacterial problems.
A strobilurin used alone: blast in Asia has already learned to survive this group. A last resort.
A strobilurin used alone: blast in Asia has already learned to survive this group. A last resort.

prevent: Plant a blast resistant variety, and sow clean, healthy seed early, soon after the rains begin.
Split nitrogen into two or more doses and never pile it on.
Keep water on the field. Fields that dry out, above all rainfed ones, get much more blast.
Avoid close planting, and stay out of the crop while the leaves are wet.
On soils short of silicon, add calcium silicate or clean, blast free straw.
After a blast year, plow the stubble under at once, and rotate with mungo, corn or vegetables when you can.
bio: Bacillus and Trichoderma products give only mild help. Resistant seed and water do far more.
diseases.threshold: From tillering, check 20 hills a week for spindle shaped gray spots, more often after cool nights with long dew. Spray only when a susceptible variety meets wet, cloudy weather near heading, the field had neck blast before, or leaf blast showed at tillering: once as panicles start to emerge and again at about half heading.
diseases.rotate: Blast fungus in Japan and Vietnam already resists strobilurins (FRAC 11). Never spray group 11 alone or twice in a row. Rotate it with tricyclazole (16.1) or isoprothiolane (6), and pair it with a triazole (3).

diseases.name: Bacterial leaf blight
diseases.local: Nauga nga dahon and natala nga tanum (Cebuano), nadurot nga tanum (Waray), naggapula (Ilonggo), and kresek for the seedling wilt
diseases.hint: Yellow to orange stripes that start at the leaf tip or edge and move down with a wavy margin.
diseases.no: No spray cures it: the bacteria live inside the leaf veins, and copper only slows the spread a little.

rice: Only slows spread on the leaf surface. It cannot cure sick plants. Can scorch rice at flowering.
Only slows spread on the leaf surface. It cannot cure sick plants. Can scorch rice at flowering.
A copper made for rice bacterial diseases. It slows the spread when used early but cures nothing.
Only slows spread on the leaf surface. It cannot cure sick plants. Can scorch rice at flowering.
A friendly bacterium. Mild help at best, and only before the disease spreads.
Harsh on rice leaves and only slows the spread a little. A last resort.

avoid: Fosetyl aluminium
Made for water molds. It does not control this bacterium.
Streptomycin plus oxytetracycline
Medical antibiotics: farm use breeds bacteria that resist them, and the blight sits inside the leaf veins.
prevent: Plant a resistant variety, and change to another resistant variety if blight starts to break through.
Use clean seed from a healthy crop, and do not cut or bruise seedlings at pulling and transplanting.
Split nitrogen, never heavy, and keep potash enough. Lush, nitrogen rich rice is hit hardest.
Drain the field when blight shows, and keep water from a sick field from flowing into yours.
After harvest, plow under stubble, ratoons and volunteer rice, and keep grassy weeds off the bunds and canals.
Use wider spacing where blight is common, so leaves dry faster after rain.
bio: Bacillus products help a little as prevention. They do not cure a sick crop.
diseases.threshold: Scout from tillering, and right after storms, floods or strong winds, for wavy yellow stripes from the leaf tip or edge and milky drops on the leaf in the morning. At the first signs, act with water and fertilizer: drain the field, hold back nitrogen and add potash. Sprays will not turn it around.

diseases.name: Rice tungro
diseases.sci: Rice tungro bacilliform virus and rice tungro spherical virus
diseases.hint: Leaves that turn yellow or orange yellow, starting at the tip and spreading down the blade.
diseases.no: No spray cures tungro. Pull out sick hills, plant resistant varieties and plant together after a fallow.
avoid: Pymetrozine
A spray cannot cure tungro, and pymetrozine is weak on the green leafhopper. See the leafhopper's own list.
Buprofezin
Kills leafhopper nymphs only, not the winged adults that bring tungro in. It cannot cure the virus.
prevent: Plant a tungro resistant or leafhopper resistant variety where tungro has struck, and change varieties every few seasons.
Plant together across the barangay after a fallow, and avoid the weeks when leafhoppers peaked before.
Plow under stubble, ratoons and volunteer rice right after harvest. They carry the virus to the next crop.
Pull and bury sick hills early, and never take seedlings from a seedbed that shows yellow orange plants.
Do not plant next to a field that has tungro, and keep nitrogen at the right rate.
bio: Spiders, mirid bugs, dragonflies and damselflies eat green leafhoppers. Avoid early sprays so they stay.
diseases.threshold: Watch the seedbed and the first 40 days for hills that turn yellow to orange from the leaf tips, stay short and make few tillers, with green leafhoppers on them. Pull and bury sick hills at once. Once tungro is in the area a leafhopper spray rarely stops it, so ask a technician before you spray.

diseases.name: Brown spot of rice
diseases.hint: Small, circular, dark brown to purple brown spots on the leaves from tillering on.

rice: Spray only if the spots keep coming after you fix the seed and soil. Do not use group 11 twice in a row.
A contact protectant: it guards new leaves and the panicle but cannot heal spots already there.
A contact protectant: it guards new leaves and the panicle but cannot heal spots already there.
A contact protectant: it guards new leaves and the panicle but cannot heal spots already there.
Weak on the brown spot fungus. A triazole mix or a protectant does better.

prevent: Use clean seed, or treat your own seed in hot water at 53 to 54 degrees Celsius for 10 to 12 minutes, after an 8 hour cold soak.
Test the soil and give what it lacks, above all potash, and silicon on poor soils.
Keep water on the field where you can. Brown spot is worst in dry, unflooded soil.
Remove volunteer rice, crop debris and weeds that carry the fungus between seasons.
Plant a resistant variety, above all in direct seeded or rainfed fields.
bio: Seed treated with Trichoderma, where sold, gives seedlings a cleaner start.
diseases.threshold: Brown spot is a sign of hungry or dry soil more than a reason to spray. Check 20 hills from tillering. Spray only if spots keep spreading to the upper leaves and the flag leaf after you fix the soil, or the field had spotted grain before, at booting to heading.

diseases.name: False smut
diseases.hint: A few grains on a panicle swell into balls that are over twice the size of a normal grain.
prevent: Use clean, certified seed. If unsure, treat it in hot water at 52 degrees Celsius for 10 minutes before sowing.
Keep nitrogen moderate and split it. Heavy nitrogen before heading invites the fungus.
Avoid close planting, and alternate flooding and drying where you can, to cut humidity in the crop.
Pick smut balls as soon as you see them, before they turn green black, and carry them out in a bag.
After harvest, remove or plow under straw and stubble, and time planting so flowering misses the rainiest weeks.
diseases.threshold: You cannot wait for the balls to decide: by then a spray is too late. Decide at late booting: spray only in a field that had false smut before, when humid, cloudy or rainy weather is forecast for flowering.

diseases.name: Bacterial leaf streak
diseases.hint: Narrow, water soaked streaks run between the veins of the leaf, with straight sides.
diseases.no: No product cures it. Clean seed, resistant varieties and drainage keep it out. Copper only slows it a little.

rice: Only slows spread on the leaf surface after draining. It cures nothing. Can scorch rice at flowering.
Only slows spread on the leaf surface after draining. It cures nothing. Can scorch rice at flowering.
Only slows spread on the leaf surface after draining. It cures nothing. Can scorch rice at flowering.

prevent: Sow certified seed of a variety that has held up in your area, and never save seed from a field that had streak.
Pull out grassy weeds around the field and in the bunds. The bacterium lives on them between crops.
Split nitrogen into small doses and add potash in splits, so leaves stay firm and harder to wound.
Drain the field when streak shows, and do not let water from sick fields flow into healthy ones.
After harvest, plow under or remove the stubble, and rotate with another crop when you can.
diseases.threshold: Scout during tillering in wet, windy weeks for narrow, water soaked streaks between the veins that turn yellow with tiny amber drops. At the first streaks, drain the field and hold back nitrogen. A copper spray comes only after that, and only if the streaks keep spreading.

diseases.name: Sheath rot
diseases.hint: Oblong or irregular spots form on the top leaf sheath, with dark reddish brown edges and gray centers.

rice: Spray at booting where sheath rot was bad before. Once the panicle is stuck, a spray cannot free it.
A protectant with only mild effect on sheath rot, and copper can scorch the emerging panicle.

prevent: Use healthy seed from a field free of the disease, and treat the seed before sowing if the field had sheath rot.
Do not plant too close. Sheath rot rises with planting density.
Split the nitrogen and add potash instead of more nitrogen.
Control stem borers and sheath mites, whose wounds let the fungus in, but keep insecticides off for the first 30 to 40 days.
Remove infected stubble and crop residue after harvest, and plow it under.
diseases.threshold: From booting, check the flag leaf sheath on 20 hills for oblong spots with gray centers and brown edges, and for panicles that fail to come out. Spray at booting only in fields with a history of sheath rot. After the panicle is trapped it is too late.

diseases.name: Narrow brown leaf spot
diseases.hint: Thin, straight brown lines run parallel to the veins on the leaf and the upper sheath.

rice: Rarely needed: the disease is usually minor. Spray only a susceptible variety at panicle initiation or early boot.
Rarely needed: the disease is usually minor. Spray only a susceptible variety at panicle initiation or early boot.
Rarely needed. Fungi learn to survive this group quickly, so use it once and rotate.
Weak on this leaf spot, and copper can scorch rice at heading.

prevent: Test the soil and fix a potassium shortage with potash. The disease follows potassium poor soils.
Use certified seed of a variety that shows less of the disease.
Follow the recommended nitrogen rate, or the leaf color chart, so you do not overfeed.
Keep weeds down in the field and on the bunds, and add organic matter to build the soil.
Plant at the best time for your area, and clear diseased straw and stubble after harvest.
diseases.threshold: Usually minor. Check the upper leaves and sheaths from panicle initiation. A spray pays only on a susceptible variety when thin brown streaks spread onto the flag leaf before heading.

diseases.name: Rice grassy stunt
diseases.hint: Plants are severely stunted, with many thin tillers and a grassy, rosette look.
diseases.no: No spray cures the virus. Fight the brown planthopper that carries it, with resistant seed and planting together first.
prevent: Plant a variety that resists the brown planthopper, or the virus, or both.
Plant together with the farms around you and keep a fallow, so hoppers cannot move from old fields onto young ones.
Pull out and bury sick plants early, and plow under stubble, ratoons and volunteer rice after harvest.
Flood the seedbed for a day when planthoppers are on it, so they drown.
No insecticide in the first 30 to 40 days, and never a pyrethroid: both bring planthoppers back worse.
Avoid close planting, and leave a narrow walking gap every few meters to scout.
bio: Spiders, mirid bugs, water striders and egg wasps keep planthoppers in check. Spare them by not spraying early.
diseases.threshold: Where grassy stunt showed before, tap 20 hills a week for brown planthoppers from the seedbed through tillering, and look for stunted hills with many thin, upright, pale tillers. The virus spreads at hopper counts far below hopperburn, so pull sick hills at once and use only the selective hopper sprays when counts climb.

diseases.name: Rice ragged stunt
diseases.hint: Plants are severely stunted in the early growth stages, with short, dark green leaves.
diseases.no: No spray cures the virus. Fight the brown planthopper that carries it, with resistant seed and planting together first.
prevent: Plant a resistant variety: some resist the planthopper, some the virus, some both.
Plant at the same time as the farms around you, and leave a fallow or rotate so volunteer rice does not keep the virus.
Pull out and bury sick plants early, and destroy infected stubble and crop residue after harvest.
Flood the seedbed for a day when planthoppers are on it, so they drown.
No insecticide in the first 30 to 40 days, and never a pyrethroid: both bring planthoppers back worse.
bio: Spiders, mirid bugs and egg wasps eat planthoppers. Spare them by not spraying early.
diseases.threshold: Where ragged stunt showed before, tap 20 hills a week for brown planthoppers from the seedbed through tillering, and look for short, dark green hills with ragged, twisted leaf edges. The virus spreads at hopper counts far below hopperburn, so pull sick hills at once and use only the selective hopper sprays when counts climb.

diseases.name: Bakanae
diseases.hint: Seedlings several inches taller than their neighbors, thin and arching over the healthy plants.
diseases.no: A spray on the standing crop does not help. Treat the seed before sowing and pull the sick plants.
prevent: Buy certified, clean seed, and never save seed from a field that had tall, pale plants.
Float the seed in salt water or plain water and throw away the light seeds that float.
Soak seed you trust in hot water at 55 to 57 degrees Celsius before sowing. It fails on heavily infected seed.
Pull the tall seedlings out of the seedbed and the field, and bury them away from the paddy.
Plow in the straw and stubble right after harvest, and rotate away from rice for two years after a bad outbreak.
bio: Seed treated with Trichoderma, where sold, lowers bakanae a little.
diseases.threshold: Check the seedbed and the young field every week for seedlings taller, thinner and paler than the rest. Pull and bury them at once, before they shed spores at flowering. A few sick plants in a hundred is reason to change the seed source next season.
diseases.rotate: Bakanae fungus in China, Japan and Korea has resisted benzimidazoles (carbendazim, thiophanate methyl) after long seed treatment use. Pair them with thiram or captan, and switch seed source when bakanae keeps coming back.

diseases.name: Rice stem rot
diseases.hint: Small, irregular black spots on the outer leaf sheath at the waterline.

rice: A contact protectant with little effect on stem rot at the waterline. Drainage, potash and stubble removal do more.

prevent: Destroy the hard black resting bodies after harvest: plow straw and stubble deep, or remove them, and let the field dry.
Balance the fertilizer: too much nitrogen with too little potassium raises stem rot. Split doses of potash lower it.
Drain the field now and then during the crop, since floodwater carries the floating resting bodies.
Control stem borers and planthoppers that wound the stem, but keep sprays off for the first 30 to 40 days.
Rotate with a legume or forage crop when you can, since no variety is highly resistant.
diseases.threshold: From late tillering, part 20 hills and look at the outer sheath at the waterline for small black spots that grow and darken the stem. A spray seldom pays. In a field with a clear history of stem rot, act at the first lesions with drainage and potash, and spray only on a technician's advice.

diseases.name: Corn downy mildew
diseases.hint: Pale or yellow stripes on the first true leaves of young seedlings.

diseases.name: Corn rust
diseases.hint: Small, round to oval pustules on the leaves, brown, orange or brick red.

diseases.name: Northern corn leaf blight
diseases.hint: Long, narrow tan lesions along the leaf edge on the lower leaves, the first sign.

diseases.name: Banded leaf and sheath blight
diseases.hint: Water soaked, discolored bands and rings on the leaf sheaths, brown, tan or gray.

diseases.name: Corn stalk rot
diseases.sci: Fusarium spp., Pythium aphanidermatum, Dickeya zeae
diseases.hint: Plants that wilt or turn gray and brown while the grain is filling.
diseases.no: No fungicide is labeled for stalk rot. Feed, space and drain the crop well.

diseases.name: Corn ear rot
diseases.hint: Pinkish white, cottony or powdery growth on the cob and between kernels, the sign of Fusarium.

diseases.name: Bacterial wilt
diseases.hint: Sudden wilting of the whole plant while the leaves are still green.
diseases.no: No spray works. The bacteria live inside the plant, out of reach.

diseases.name: Damping off
diseases.sci: Pythium spp., Rhizoctonia solani, Fusarium spp.
diseases.hint: Gaps in the seedbed because seeds rotted before they sprouted.

diseases.name: Early blight
diseases.sci: Alternaria solani (on tomato also named Alternaria linariae)
diseases.hint: Small brown spots with yellow edges appear first on the oldest, lowest leaves.

diseases.name: Late blight
diseases.hint: Brown or black patches start at the leaf tips and edges and spread fast across the veins.

diseases.name: Powdery mildew
diseases.sci: Podosphaera xanthii, Erysiphe spp., Leveillula taurica
diseases.hint: Round white spots, like flour, appear on the leaves, the leaf stalks and the stems.

diseases.name: Downy mildew of cucurbits
diseases.hint: Yellow spots appear on older leaves, round at first, then angular between the veins.

diseases.name: Clubroot
diseases.hint: Plants droop even though the soil is still wet.

diseases.name: Black rot of cabbage
diseases.hint: Yellow to brown V shaped patches start at the leaf edge.

diseases.name: Bacterial soft rot
diseases.hint: Water soaked spots appear on outer leaves, stems, heads or fruit, then grow and sink.
diseases.no: Sprays do not stop soft rot. The steps on its page do.

diseases.name: Tomato leaf curl
diseases.hint: The leaf edges curl upward and inward, and the leaflets are small and puckered.
diseases.no: No spray cures the virus. Control the whitefly and plant resistant varieties.

diseases.name: Cercospora leaf spot
diseases.sci: Cercospora spp. (for example C. citrullina on cucurbits and C. beticola on beet and spinach)
diseases.hint: Small, round spots appear on the older leaves first.

diseases.name: Purple blotch of onion
diseases.hint: Small, sunken spots with a white center appear on the leaves.

diseases.name: Root knot nematode
diseases.sci: Meloidogyne spp. (Meloidogyne incognita, Meloidogyne graminicola and others)
diseases.hint: Plants stay stunted and uneven across the field, often in patches.

diseases.name: Anthracnose
diseases.hint: Black, sunken spots on ripening fruit, rotting sili pods and twisted onion leaves.

diseases.name: Fusarium wilt
diseases.hint: Older leaves yellow and wilt, with brown streaks inside the stem.
diseases.no: No fungicide cures it. Plant resistant varieties and keep the fungus out of clean soil.

diseases.name: Banana bunchy top
diseases.hint: New leaves come out narrow, short and stiff, and they crowd together at the top of the plant.

diseases.name: Black sigatoka
diseases.hint: Small reddish brown flecks appear first on the underside of young leaves.

diseases.name: Moko disease and bugtok of banana
diseases.local: Bugtok is also called tapurok, in saba and cardaba.
diseases.hint: On Cavendish and other dessert bananas, leaves turn yellow and then wilt.
diseases.no: No spray cures it. Disinfect your tools with dilute bleach.

diseases.name: Papaya ringspot
diseases.hint: The leaves get a mottled mosaic of bright yellow and green.
diseases.no: Insecticide sprays rarely help. Aphids pass the virus on before a spray can kill them.

diseases.name: Coconut cadang cadang
diseases.local: In Bicol the disease is called gadan gadan, which means dead or dying.
diseases.hint: Yellow, or chlorotic, spots appear on the leaves.
diseases.no: No spray cures it. Remove sick palms and clean your tools.

diseases.name: Coconut bud rot
diseases.hint: The spear leaf wilts or bends over, and may turn light green.

diseases.name: Citrus greening
diseases.hint: Leaves show a blotchy mottle, with yellow and green patches in an uneven pattern.

diseases.name: Black pod of cacao
diseases.hint: Small brown, oily spots appear on the pod and spread quickly.

diseases.name: Coffee leaf rust
diseases.hint: Small spots of about 2 to 3 mm appear and grow to about 15 mm.

diseases.name: Southern corn leaf blight
diseases.hint: Small tan to brown oblong spots between the leaf veins that join into large dead patches across the leaf.

sources.label: DA Caraga Corn Program, Mga Kasagarang Sakit sa Mais (Technoguide 27, 2021)

diseases.name: Grain mold of sorghum
diseases.sci: Fusarium spp., Curvularia lunata, Alternaria spp. and other fungi
diseases.hint: Grains turn pink, white and fluffy, or black when rain falls during flowering and grain filling, and they crumble at threshing.

sources.label: TNAU Agritech, Grain mould of sorghum

diseases.name: Southern blight (stem rot)
diseases.hint: A branch or the whole plant wilts, and white cottony threads with small round seed like balls cover the stem at the soil line.

sources.label: Pacific Pests and Pathogens, Peanut southern blight
PhilFIDA, Technoguide on Cotton Pests and their Management
EWS Plant Doctor, Southern blight
DA RFO 02, Tomato Production Guide

diseases.name: Stem rot and charcoal rot
diseases.hint: Dark brown sunken patches circle the stem near the soil, peppered with tiny black dots, and the plant wilts and breaks.

sources.label: FAO AGRIS: IPM module against stem rot and insect pests of jute (Corchorus olitorius)

diseases.name: Bean rust
diseases.hint: Raised reddish brown pustules ringed with yellow form on the leaf underside and rub off as a rusty powder.

sources.label: DA RFO 02 Cagayan Valley, Snap Beans Production Guide

diseases.name: Bean and cowpea mosaic
diseases.sci: Bean common mosaic virus, Cowpea aphid borne mosaic virus
diseases.hint: Leaves show light and dark green patches, pucker and curl down, and the pods are few and twisted.
diseases.no: Sprays do not help, because aphids pass the virus on before an insecticide kills them. Plant clean seed, pull out sick plants early and keep new plantings away from old ones.

sources.label: Pacific Pests and Pathogens, Bean common mosaic

diseases.name: Early and late leaf spot of peanut
diseases.hint: Brown spots with a yellow ring, or dark brown to black spots on the leaf underside, and the leaves drop early.

sources.label: Peanut CRSP Philippines, Peanut production guide (M. K. Palomar, editor)

diseases.name: Peanut rust
diseases.hint: Tiny orange to reddish brown pustules under the older leaves break open and shed a rusty powder.

sources.label: Peanut CRSP Philippines, Peanut production guide (M. K. Palomar, editor)

diseases.name: Soybean rust
diseases.hint: Tiny tan to reddish brown spots with raised pustules on the underside of the lower leaves, which yellow and drop early.

sources.label: Asian soybean rust review, notes yield losses up to 80 percent in the Philippines (PMC)

diseases.name: False rust of winged bean (orange gall)
diseases.hint: Small bright orange yellow raised galls cover the leaves, stems and pods, which twist and curl when badly hit.
diseases.no: No spray is proven against it. Plant tolerant varieties, pick off galled parts, space the vines for air and save seed only from clean plants.

sources.label: PROSEA, Psophocarpus tetragonolobus (winged bean)
PestNet, false rust (Synchytrium psophocarpi) on winged bean

diseases.name: Pigeon pea wilt
diseases.hint: Plants yellow and wilt one by one, often at flowering and podding, with a purple band at the stem base and brown streaks inside the stem.

sources.label: Journal of Biological Control, Management of pigeonpea wilt caused by Fusarium udum through integrated approaches

diseases.name: Storage rot of root crops
diseases.sci: Lasiodiplodia theobromae, Fusarium spp., Penicillium spp., Rhizopus stolonifer
diseases.hint: Stored tubers and roots soften, turn brown or black inside and grow white, green or black mold, starting at cuts and bruises.
diseases.no: Sprays do not save stored tubers; dig with care, cure them in the shade for a few days, keep only sound ones, and store dry and airy.

sources.label: PROSEA: Dioscorea alata (purple yam)
DA RFO 2 Sweet Potato Production Guide

diseases.name: Rhizome and corm rot
diseases.sci: Pythium aphanidermatum, Pythium myriotylum and other Pythium spp. (often with Fusarium spp.)
diseases.hint: Lower leaves yellow, shoots fall over at the collar, and the rhizome or corm turns soft, watery, brown and foul smelling.

sources.label: DA CAR Technoguide: production and management of ginger
Vikaspedia: pests and diseases management in ginger

diseases.name: Sweet potato scab
diseases.hint: Small corky brown scabs form on leaf veins and vines, and young leaves curl, twist and stay small.

sources.label: DA RFO 2 Sweet Potato Production Guide
Pacific Pests, Pathogens and Weeds: Sweetpotato scab

diseases.name: Sweet potato virus disease
diseases.sci: Virus complex: sweet potato feathery mottle virus, sweet potato chlorotic stunt virus and others
diseases.hint: Leaves show vein clearing, mosaic or purple veins, turn small, crinkled and misshapen, and vines are stunted with short joints.
diseases.no: No spray cures a virus; plant virus free cuttings, pull out sick plants and volunteers, and keep aphids and whiteflies down.

sources.label: DA RFO 2 Sweet Potato Production Guide

diseases.name: Sweet potato little leaf
diseases.hint: Vines turn bushy with many side shoots and tiny pale leaves, and the plant forms few or no roots.
diseases.no: No spray cures it; plant cuttings only from healthy fields, pull and burn bushy plants, and do not plant beside a sick field.

sources.label: Pacific Pests, Pathogens and Weeds: Sweetpotato little leaf
EPPO Global Database: sweet potato little leaf phytoplasma, Philippines

diseases.name: Cassava witches broom
diseases.sci: Phytoplasma (Candidatus Phytoplasma luffae group); the fungus Ceratobasidium theobromae is also found in sick plants
diseases.hint: Many thin shoots bunch at the top like a broom, leaves turn small and yellow, stems dry back, and roots stay small with brown streaks inside.
diseases.no: No spray cures it; plant cuttings only from healthy fields, pull and burn broomed plants, and keep mealybugs and leafhoppers down.

sources.label: Status of Cassava Witches Broom Disease in the Philippines (Plants, 2024)

diseases.name: Taro leaf blight
diseases.hint: Round purple brown spots with a yellow edge ooze yellow drops and spread fast in rainy weather until the whole leaf collapses.

sources.label: Pacific Pests, Pathogens and Weeds: Taro leaf blight

diseases.name: Potato cyst nematode
diseases.hint: Plants grow in stunted yellow patches that wilt at midday, and pinhead sized white to golden cysts cling to the roots.

sources.label: Benguet State University policy brief: potato cyst nematode and bacterial wilt in Benguet
BPI Baguio addresses bacterial wilt and potato cyst nematode

diseases.name: Carrot leaf blight
diseases.hint: Dark brown spots with yellow edges start on older leaves and stalks, then join until the tops blacken and dry as if scorched.

sources.label: Pacific Pests, Pathogens and Weeds: Carrot leaf spot

diseases.name: Ginger leaf spot
diseases.hint: Small water soaked spots on the leaves grow into yellowish then brown spots with white centers that run together.

sources.label: Vikaspedia: pests and diseases management in ginger

diseases.name: Mosaic viruses of squash and gourds
diseases.sci: Zucchini yellow mosaic virus, Papaya ringspot virus type W, Cucumber mosaic virus, Watermelon mosaic virus; on sayote, Chayote mosaic virus
diseases.hint: Leaves turn mottled yellow and green with blisters, stay small and twisted, and fruits come out bumpy or spotted.
diseases.no: No spray cures a virus. Pull and burn sick vines early, control aphids, remove weedy hosts and plant tolerant varieties.

sources.label: DA RFO 02, Squash Production Guide
EWS Plant Doctor, Zucchini yellow mosaic
NORDIS, BSU on chayote mosaic virus in Benguet

diseases.name: Alternaria leaf spot of the cabbage family
diseases.hint: Round brown to black spots with rings like a target and a yellow halo appear on older leaves, and heads may show dark specks.

sources.label: Pacific Pests, Pathogens and Weeds: Cabbage black leaf spot

diseases.name: Thrips borne mottle and spotted wilt viruses
diseases.sci: Watermelon silver mottle virus, Melon yellow spot virus, Tomato spotted wilt virus (tospoviruses)
diseases.hint: Leaves show pale flecks, rings or silvery mottling, shoot tips stand up stiff, and plants infected young stay small and bear little.
diseases.no: No spray cures the virus. Control thrips early, pull sick plants, and clear weeds and old crop debris after harvest.

sources.label: EWS Plant Doctor, Tospovirus
EWS Plant Doctor, Watermelon diseases and pests

diseases.name: White rust
diseases.sci: Albugo candida (cabbage family), Albugo ipomoeae aquaticae (kangkong)
diseases.hint: Raised white blisters under the leaves burst into white powder, with yellow patches above and twisted, swollen shoots.

sources.label: Pacific Pests, Pathogens and Weeds: Cabbage white rust (also kangkong)

diseases.name: Phytophthora blight
diseases.hint: Black lesions climb the stem from the base, the crown rots and the whole plant wilts, and fruits rot under white mold in wet weather.

sources.label: EWS Plant Doctor, Phytophthora blight
EWS Plant Doctor, Eggplant diseases and pests

diseases.name: Choanephora wet rot
diseases.hint: Flowers and young fruits turn soft and wet, then grow whiskers of fungus with tiny black heads, like a pincushion.

sources.label: EWS Plant Doctor, Choanephora wet rot
EWS Plant Doctor, Eggplant diseases and pests
DA RFO 02, Upo Production Guide

diseases.name: Gummy stem blight
diseases.hint: Brown V shaped spots start at the leaf edge, and the stem near the base gets long brown lesions that crack and ooze gum.

sources.label: EWS Plant Doctor, Gummy stem blight
EWS Plant Doctor, Watermelon diseases and pests

diseases.name: Mosaic virus of tomato and pepper
diseases.sci: Tobacco mosaic virus and Tomato mosaic virus (tobamoviruses)
diseases.hint: Young leaves show light and dark green mottling, turn narrow and twisted, and the plant stays stunted.
diseases.no: No spray cures it. Uproot sick plants, wash hands and tools, and never smoke while handling seedlings.

sources.label: DA RFO 02, Tomato Production Guide
ATI CAR, Tomato Production leaflet
EWS Plant Doctor, Tobacco and tomato mosaic

diseases.name: Bacterial spot
diseases.sci: Xanthomonas spp. (Xanthomonas euvesicatoria, Xanthomonas perforans and relatives)
diseases.hint: Small water soaked spots on the leaves turn brown with dead centers, and fruits get raised, rough, scabby spots.

sources.label: EWS Plant Doctor, Bacterial spot
DA RFO 02, Tomato Production Guide

diseases.name: Gray mold
diseases.hint: Berries get soft brown spots, often under the green cap, that grow a gray dusty mold.

sources.label: UC IPM, Botrytis fruit rot of strawberry
Benguet State University, Disease management strategies in strawberry production in Benguet

diseases.name: Mosaic of tobacco (TMV and CMV)
diseases.sci: Tobacco mosaic virus (TMV), Cucumber mosaic virus (CMV)
diseases.hint: Leaves show light and dark green patches, pucker and twist, and the plants grow slowly.
diseases.no: No spray cures them. TMV spreads on hands and tools, so wash hands with soap and do not smoke while working, and CMV comes with aphids. Pull out sick plants early.

sources.label: AGRIS, Pest clinic: a link among NTA researchers, extensionists and farmers

diseases.name: Bacterial leaf spot of lettuce
diseases.sci: Xanthomonas hortorum pv. vitians (Xanthomonas campestris pv. vitians)
diseases.hint: Small water soaked spots turn angular and black between the veins, dry out papery, and heads can rot from the outer leaves.

sources.label: Nordis: new crop diseases found in Benguet (lettuce bacterial leaf spot)

diseases.name: Septoria late blight of celery
diseases.hint: Small yellow spots turn brown with tiny black dots inside and spread over leaves and stalks until the leaves dry up.

sources.label: Texas Plant Disease Handbook: celery
Pacific Pests, Pathogens and Weeds: Celery early blight

diseases.name: Strawberry leaf spot
diseases.hint: Small deep purple spots appear on the leaves, their centers turn gray to white, and many spots merge and kill the leaf.

sources.label: UC IPM, Common leaf spot of strawberry
Benguet State University, Disease management strategies in strawberry production in Benguet

diseases.name: Verticillium wilt
diseases.hint: Outer leaves brown along the edges and between the veins and collapse, while the inner leaves stay green and the plant stays small.
diseases.no: No spray cures it. Rotate with broccoli, plant clean runners of tolerant varieties, and avoid fields where it struck before.

sources.label: UC IPM, Verticillium wilt of strawberry
Benguet State University, Disease management strategies in strawberry production in Benguet

diseases.name: Stemphylium leaf blight
diseases.hint: Small pale yellow water soaked spots on the leaves grow into long tan to brown blotches that dry the leaves from the tips.

sources.label: East West Seed Plant Doctor: onion diseases and pests
Review: Stemphylium vesicarium, an onion pathogen, and options for suppression

diseases.name: Anthracnose twister of onion
diseases.sci: Colletotrichum gloeosporioides with Fusarium spp. (Gibberella moniliformis)
diseases.hint: Leaves twist and curl, the neck grows long and thin, pale sunken spots with tiny dark dots appear, and bulbs stay small or rot.

sources.label: DOST PCAARRD: UPLB work on onion anthracnose twister
DA Ilocos: help for onion farms hit by armyworm and anthracnose

diseases.name: Yellow stripe and dwarf viruses of onion and garlic
diseases.sci: Onion yellow dwarf virus, leek yellow stripe virus, shallot yellow stripe virus and garlic latent viruses
diseases.hint: Leaves show yellow streaks or stripes, turn flat, crinkled and floppy, and plants and bulbs stay small.
diseases.no: No spray cures a virus; plant clean cloves and sets, pull streaked plants early, and keep aphids and thrips down.

sources.label: East West Seed Plant Doctor: onion diseases and pests
FAO AGRIS: garlic transcriptome and the viruses threatening Philippine garlic

diseases.name: Pineapple disease and butt rot
diseases.hint: Planting pieces turn red then black inside from the cut ends and smell like ripe pineapple, and the shoots die or stay stunted and yellow.

sources.label: Kerala Agricultural University, Sugarcane sett rot

diseases.name: Ganoderma basal stem rot
diseases.hint: Several unopened spear leaves pile up, the old fronds yellow and droop, and hard brown brackets grow on the lower trunk.
diseases.no: No fungicide saves a sick palm. Dig out and chop infected stumps and roots at replanting, and drain and feed the palms well.

sources.label: Pacific Pests and Pathogens, Oil palm basal stem rot

diseases.name: Sugarcane smut
diseases.hint: A long black whip covered in a thin silvery skin grows out of the top of the stalk and sheds black powder.
diseases.no: No spray cures it. Plant resistant varieties and clean, hot water treated setts, and bag and burn the whips before they shed spores.

sources.label: JIRCAS, Selected Economically Important Diseases of Some Major Crops in the Philippines

diseases.name: Leaf scald of sugarcane
diseases.hint: Thin white pencil lines run along the leaves, the leaves later dry from the tips, and side shoots sprout along the stalk.
diseases.no: Sprays do little once the cane is infected. Plant clean setts of resistant varieties and disinfect cane knives between stools.

sources.label: Recent advances in sugarcane leaf scald disease (PMC)

diseases.name: Heart rot and root rot of pineapple
diseases.hint: The young leaves in the center turn yellow brown, rot at the base and pull out easily with a foul smell.

sources.label: Visayas State University, Major Diseases of Queen Pineapple

diseases.name: Black shank of tobacco
diseases.hint: Plants wilt and stunt, the roots blacken and rot, and the stem turns black from the base, with the dried pith inside often split into discs.

sources.label: AGRIS, Isolation and pathogenicity of Phytophthora from tobacco in Philippine tobacco areas

diseases.name: Bacterial blight of cotton (angular leaf spot)
diseases.hint: Angular, water soaked spots between the leaf veins turn brown and black, with black streaks along the veins and stems.

sources.label: PhilFIDA, Technoguide on Cotton Pests and their Management

diseases.name: Abaca mosaic
diseases.hint: Light green to yellow streaks and stripes run along the leaf blade, and the plant grows smaller.
diseases.no: No spray cures it. Spray the aphids on plants within six meters, then rogue the sick mat and replant with clean planting material.

sources.label: DA HVCDP, Giya sa Pagpananum ug Abaca (Technoguide 05, 2019)
JIRCAS, Selected Economically Important Diseases of Some Major Crops in the Philippines

diseases.name: Abaca bract mosaic
diseases.hint: Leaves curl and roll upward, and the leaf stalks and sheaths show spindle shaped streaks like a cucumber skin.
diseases.no: No spray cures it. Rogue sick plants, keep aphids down and plant only clean, virus free planting material.

sources.label: DA HVCDP, Giya sa Pagpananum ug Abaca (Technoguide 05, 2019)

diseases.name: Corynespora leaf fall
diseases.hint: Brown spots with a yellow halo and darkened veins that look like fish bones, and the leaves yellow and fall out of season.

sources.label: DOST PCAARRD, USM study on leaf diseases of rubber in North Cotabato

diseases.name: Bamboo witches broom
diseases.sci: Candidatus Phytoplasma luffae related strain (16SrVIII) in the Philippines, while the fungus Aciculosporium take causes a similar broom elsewhere
diseases.hint: Leaves bunch into rosettes, many thin limbs sprout from one node and the internodes stay short, like a broom.
diseases.no: No spray cures it. Cut and burn the broomed branches and culms, and take planting material only from healthy clumps.

sources.label: Philippine Journal of Science, Distribution of bamboo witches broom disease in the Philippines

diseases.name: Pestalotiopsis leaf fall
diseases.sci: Pestalotiopsis spp. (Pestalotiopsis microspora and other species)
diseases.hint: Round brown spots with a pale yellow ring appear on mature leaves, then the leaves yellow and drop until the canopy is thin and latex output falls.

sources.label: DOST PCAARRD, Addressing the Pestalotiopsis leaf fall disease in rubber trees in Mindanao
Journal News, More funds for treatment of infected rubber plantations in BARMM
Philippine Rubber Research Institute, Pestalotiopsis leaf fall disease in Basilan

diseases.name: Curvularia leaf spot
diseases.hint: Small yellow spots on young nursery seedlings turn brown with a yellow ring and join into dry patches, and badly hit seedlings stunt or die.
diseases.no: No fungicide for this nursery disease is listed in Philippine guides; space the seedlings, water at the base in the morning, and cut off and burn spotted leaves.

sources.label: Prince of Songkla University, Curvularia leaf spot of oil palm seedlings (2016)

diseases.name: Sooty mold
diseases.sci: Capnodium mangiferae, Capnodium ramosum and other sooty mold fungi
diseases.hint: A black velvety coat like soot covers leaves, flowers and fruit wherever leafhoppers, scales or mealybugs drip sticky honeydew.
diseases.no: Spraying the black coat does little; control the honeydew insects (leafhoppers, scales, mealybugs, aphids), prune for air and light, and the mold fades.

sources.label: DA Caraga HVCDP, Giya sa pagpananum ug manga
BPI, Mangosteen production guide

diseases.name: Pink disease
diseases.hint: White cobweb threads, then a pink crust, cover the branches near the forks, and the leaves above die but stay hanging.

sources.label: Pacific Pests and Pathogens, Pink disease of cocoa
DA HVCDP and BPI DNCRDC, Durian production guide

diseases.name: Phytophthora patch canker, foot rot and fruit rot
diseases.hint: Wet dark patches on the trunk bark ooze reddish brown gum, seedlings die back, and fruits get water soaked spots that turn brown, crack and rot.

sources.label: BPI, Durian production guide
DA HVCDP and BPI DNCRDC, Durian production guide
DOST PCAARRD, ACIAR jackfruit project on Phytophthora

diseases.name: Algal leaf spot
diseases.hint: Fuzzy round green to orange spots on the upper side of the leaves, and black rough spots on guava fruit.
diseases.no: Sprays are not a fitting control; prune low branches, open the canopy to light and air, drain wet ground, and feed the trees well.

sources.label: Pacific Pests and Pathogens, Algal leaf spot

diseases.name: White root rot
diseases.hint: Leaves lose their gloss, turn yellow, curl down and fall, and thick white threads cover the roots and the collar, with orange brackets at the base later.

sources.label: Rubber Research Institute of Sri Lanka, Management of White Root Disease

diseases.name: Citrus tristeza
diseases.hint: Trees slowly decline with small yellowing leaves, twig dieback and pits in the wood under the bark, often together with greening.
diseases.no: No spray cures it; plant certified virus free seedlings on tolerant rootstock, remove declining trees, and keep aphids down on new flushes.

sources.label: Philippine Agricultural Scientist, HLB and tristeza in Oriental Mindoro calamansi

diseases.name: Citrus foot rot and gummosis
diseases.sci: Phytophthora spp. (Phytophthora citrophthora, Phytophthora nicotianae, Phytophthora palmivora)
diseases.hint: Dark sticky gum oozes from cracked bark near the base of the trunk, the bark underneath turns brown and rots, and the canopy yellows and thins.

sources.label: ATI 4B, Calamansi production guide

diseases.name: Citrus scab
diseases.hint: Raised corky pale orange to brown warts form on young leaves, twigs and fruits, and badly hit leaves crinkle and twist.

sources.label: ATI 4B, Calamansi production guide

diseases.name: Citrus canker
diseases.hint: Raised corky brown spots with a yellow ring and an oily, glazed edge appear on leaves, twigs and fruits.

sources.label: ATI 4B, Calamansi production guide

diseases.name: Diplodia fruit rot
diseases.hint: Fruits darken to brown and black from the stem end or a wound, the flesh turns dry and corky, and black sooty spores cover the skin.

sources.label: PROSEA via Growables, Star apple diseases and pests
Horticulturae (MDPI), Lasiodiplodia and other fungi on soursop fruit

diseases.name: Burrowing nematode and root lesion nematodes of banana
diseases.sci: Radopholus similis, Pratylenchus coffeae, Pratylenchus goodeyi
diseases.hint: Roots show dark red to black lesions and snap easily, plants stay small with light bunches, and heavy plants topple over in wind or rain.

sources.label: BPI, Banana production guide
DA HVCDP, Banana production manual

diseases.name: Banana bract mosaic
diseases.hint: Spindle shaped streaks run along the leaves and leaf stalks, and the heart bracts and inner leaf sheaths show a dark reddish brown mosaic, mostly on saba and latundan.
diseases.no: No spray cures a virus; spray aphids on nearby plants first, then dig out and chop the sick mat, keep corn and weeds away, and replant clean tissue culture plantlets.

sources.label: BPI, Banana production guide
DA HVCDP, Banana production manual

diseases.name: Banana freckle
diseases.hint: Older leaves and the fruit peel get many tiny raised black dots that feel rough like sandpaper, and the blemished fruit sells poorly.

sources.label: BPI, Banana production guide
DA HVCDP, Banana production manual

diseases.name: Papaya bacterial crown rot
diseases.hint: Angular water soaked spots on leaves and leaf stalks spread into a soft rot of the crown, the top of the plant collapses, and fruits get firm sunken spots.
diseases.no: No spray reliably cures it; cut out and bury sick plants right away, avoid wounding plants, clean tools, and plant tolerant lines where available.

sources.label: UPLB, Erwinia mallotivora and papaya bacterial crown rot
ACIAR, Papaya and fruit disease final report HORT 2012 113

diseases.name: Mango scab
diseases.hint: Young fruits get grey brown corky spots that roughen and twist the skin, and leaves show brown rough spots on the underside.

sources.label: DA Caraga HVCDP, Giya sa pagpananum ug manga

diseases.name: Rhizopus fruit rot of jackfruit
diseases.hint: Male flowers and young fruits turn soft and brown, get covered with grey black fuzzy mold, and then drop.

sources.label: Vikaspedia, IPM for jackfruit pests

diseases.name: Avocado root rot
diseases.hint: Leaves turn pale, small and wilted, branches die back from the top and feeder roots are black and rotten, worst on wet poorly drained soil.

sources.label: FAO, Avocado production in the Philippines

diseases.name: Avocado scab
diseases.hint: Raised brown corky scabs form on young fruits and leaves and later merge into rough patches on the skin.

sources.label: FAO, Avocado production in the Philippines

diseases.name: Rambutan powdery mildew
diseases.hint: White powdery growth covers young flushes, flowers and young fruits, which turn brown, grow short spines, stay small and drop.

sources.label: BPI Davao, Powdery mildew of rambutan (FAO AGRIS)

diseases.name: Vascular streak dieback of cacao
diseases.hint: Leaves two or three behind the shoot tip turn yellow with small green spots and fall within days, and the branch dies back with brown streaks in the wood.
diseases.no: No spray controls it well; cut infected branches 30 cm below the streaks and burn them, thin the shade, and plant tolerant clones.

sources.label: BPI, Cacao production guide
Pacific Pests and Pathogens, Cocoa vascular streak dieback

diseases.name: Dragon fruit stem canker
diseases.hint: Small sunken white or orange spots on the stems become rusty brown corky cankers that crack and leave holes, and fruits get spots too.

sources.label: UPLB, Dragon fruit stem canker and its control

diseases.name: Chico leaf spot
diseases.hint: The leaves fill with tiny spots, pinkish to reddish brown, each with a pale whitish middle.

sources.label: National Horticulture Board India, Sapota diseases
